svg.aria-label: Map of St Hildegard's places in western Germany, numbered: 1 Bermersheim, her family home; 2 Disibodenberg, where she lived with Jutta and became magistra; 3 the Rupertsberg at Bingen, her abbey from 1150 and the place of her death in 1179; 4 Eibingen, her second abbey across the Rhine and the shrine of her relics; 5 Mainz, seat of her archbishop; 6 Ingelheim, where she met Frederick Barbarossa; 7 Trier, where Pope Eugene III read her Scivias at the synod of 1147–48 and where she preached in 1160; 8 Cologne, where she preached against the Cathars. Smaller dots mark places on her four preaching journeys: Wertheim, Würzburg, Kitzingen, Ebrach and Bamberg along the Main; Metz and Krauftal in Lorraine; Boppard, Andernach, Siegburg and Werden along the Rhine; and Maulbronn, Hirsau, Kirchheim and Zwiefalten in Swabia.
